composition.strong_posture_note: Signal profile is broadly positive — the work is protecting this position and extending reach to adjacent query types.

hook_templates.contrast: {entity_name}'s {strength_label} is one of its strongest signals — but {gap_label} is actively suppressing its AI recommendation capture.
hook_templates.problem_lead: With a {band_descriptor} (score: {score}/100), {entity_name}'s biggest exposure is in {top_gap_label}.

tier:patient_experience_reviews:strength.why: Review depth and rating are key signals AI tools use when generating provider recommendations.
tier:patient_experience_reviews:strength.say: You have {anchor_review_count} reviews at {anchor_rating} stars — that’s the social proof AI tools look for when recommending providers.

tier:patient_experience_reviews:gap.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — below the floor AI recommendation engines weight reliably.
tier:patient_experience_reviews:gap.why: This pillar captures the reputation and identity signals AI tools prioritize when generating provider recommendations; a low score here suppresses recommendation confidence directly.
tier:patient_experience_reviews:gap.say: Your {tier_label} signals are limiting your AI recommendation capture. That’s the gap we close first.

tier:credentials_recognition:strength.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — credentials and recognition signals are indexed in AI-accessible sources.
tier:credentials_recognition:strength.why: Board certifications, recognized affiliations, and clinical awards are heavily weighted by AI tools for procedural and specialist queries.
tier:credentials_recognition:strength.say: Your credentials are visible and verifiable — that’s a differentiator when AI tools rank specialists.

tier:credentials_recognition:gap.what: {entity_name}’s {tier_label} tier scores {tier_score}/100 — credentials and recognition signals are underrepresented in AI-indexable sources.
tier:credentials_recognition:gap.why: AI tools verify provider credibility through board certifications, affiliations, and awards. Missing signals here reduce recommendation confidence.
tier:credentials_recognition:gap.say: Your credentials exist but aren’t visible where it counts. We fix the indexing gap so AI tools can verify what you’ve already earned.

tier:clinical_outcomes_safety:strength.why: {top_tier_label} carries the highest pillar weight in this scoring profile — a strength here directly protects the composite.
tier:clinical_outcomes_safety:strength.say: Your strongest pillar is also the one AI tools weight most heavily — that’s a real competitive advantage.

tier:clinical_outcomes_safety:gap.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — the pillar with the most room to improve.
tier:clinical_outcomes_safety:gap.why: {top_tier_label} carries the highest pillar weight; a low score here suppresses the composite more than any other signal set.
tier:clinical_outcomes_safety:gap.say: The signals AI tools weight most heavily are the ones where {entity_name} has the most room to improve. That’s where we start.

tier:access_fit:strength.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — directory listings and access signals are consistent and well-indexed.
tier:access_fit:strength.why: Consistent NAP data and directory coverage are foundational for AI localization — they determine whether AI tools can find and verify a provider’s location.
tier:access_fit:strength.say: Your listings are clean and consistent. That’s foundational work that directly enables AI recommendation capture.

tier:access_fit:gap.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — directory listings and access signals have meaningful gaps.
tier:access_fit:gap.why: Inconsistent or incomplete name, address, or phone data across directories is a suppression signal that AI tools use to reduce recommendation confidence.
tier:access_fit:gap.say: Access & Fit signals show meaningful gaps. AI tools can’t confidently surface a provider when directory data is inconsistent or incomplete — that’s the fix we start with.

metric:physician_capture_rate:strength.what: {physician_capture_rate_pct} of {entity_name}’s physicians have verified online reviews.
metric:physician_capture_rate:strength.why: High physician capture signals a depth of reputation that AI tools surface for condition- and specialist-specific queries.
metric:physician_capture_rate:strength.say: Your physicians are individually findable online — that’s a meaningful differentiator for patients searching by condition or procedure.

metric:physician_capture_rate:gap.what: Only {physician_capture_rate_pct} of {entity_name}’s physicians have verified online reviews.
metric:physician_capture_rate:gap.why: Patients comparing providers look for individual physicians; uncaptured physicians are invisible to AI tools responding to specialist queries.
metric:physician_capture_rate:gap.say: A significant portion of your physicians don’t exist online where AI tools look. That’s referral volume your competitors can take.

metric:linkage_integrity_pct:strength.what: {entity_name}’s directory listings show strong NAP consistency — name, address, and phone data align across sources.
metric:linkage_integrity_pct:strength.why: High linkage integrity means AI tools can confidently attribute patient reviews and recommendations to the correct provider.
metric:linkage_integrity_pct:strength.say: Your listings are consistent across the web. That’s the data foundation AI tools need to recommend you without qualification.

metric:linkage_integrity_pct:gap.what: {entity_name}’s directory listings show a linkage integrity score of {linkage_integrity_pct_pct} — name, address, or phone data is not fully consistent across sources.
metric:linkage_integrity_pct:gap.why: AI systems treat NAP inconsistency as a trust signal. Conflicting data suppresses recommendation confidence and can cause misattribution to competitors.
metric:linkage_integrity_pct:gap.say: Linkage integrity is at {linkage_integrity_pct_pct} — that means directory data isn’t fully consistent across the web. AI tools use this as a confidence signal; inconsistencies cost recommendations.

metric:entity_resolution_pct:strength.what: AI tools correctly resolve queries to {entity_name} in approximately {entity_resolution_pct_pct} of standardized battery runs.
metric:entity_resolution_pct:strength.why: High entity resolution rate means AI tools reliably surface this practice when patients ask for relevant providers.
metric:entity_resolution_pct:strength.say: You’re already showing up reliably. The work now is holding that position and expanding to adjacent query types.

metric:entity_resolution_pct:gap.what: AI tools correctly resolve queries to {entity_name} in approximately {entity_resolution_pct_pct} of standardized battery runs.
metric:entity_resolution_pct:gap.why: Low resolution rate means patients asking AI tools for a provider in this category are being directed elsewhere.
metric:entity_resolution_pct:gap.say: When someone asks an AI tool for {specialty} in {city}, {entity_name} comes up less than it should. That’s the gap we close.

modifier:score_ceiling.what: A score ceiling of {ceiling_value} is currently applied — {entity_name}’s composite score cannot exceed {ceiling_value} until {score_ceiling_reason_plain}.
modifier:score_ceiling.why: The ceiling blocks all composite improvement regardless of other signal strengths. No other work moves the number until this is resolved.
modifier:score_ceiling.say: There’s a hard cap on your score right now. Nothing else we do moves the number above {ceiling_value} until one specific issue is resolved — which is exactly what we’d tackle first.

tier:_relative_strength.what: {entity_name} scores {tier_score}/100 on {tier_label} — the relative high point across all measured pillars.
tier:_relative_strength.why: Even where overall signals are developing, this pillar offers the strongest foundation for AI visibility improvements.
tier:_relative_strength.say: This is where you're furthest along — and it's the anchor for how we talk about your AI visibility profile.

composite:anchor_reputation:strength.what: {display_name}’s main listing averages {anchor_rating}★ on Google with {anchor_review_count} reviews across {n_platforms} platform(s).
composite:anchor_reputation:strength.why: Google reputation is a primary input to AI provider recommendation engines — rating and review volume directly influence whether AI tools surface this provider.
composite:anchor_reputation:strength.say: {anchor_rating} stars and {anchor_review_count} reviews — that’s a strong front door. The work now is making sure AI tools can find it reliably.

composite:anchor_reputation:gap.what: {display_name}’s primary listing shows {anchor_rating}★ across {anchor_review_count} reviews — a reputation score that works against AI recommendation capture.
composite:anchor_reputation:gap.why: AI provider recommendation engines weight primary listing rating and review volume heavily; a weak front door suppresses confidence and reduces recommendation frequency.
composite:anchor_reputation:gap.say: {anchor_rating} stars and {anchor_review_count} reviews — that’s a front door that’s working against {display_name}. AI tools lead with this signal for patient-facing queries.

demo_outcome_descriptions.mentioned: The AI tool mentions {entity_name} without a direct recommendation.

objections.objection: Our Google rating is strong — why do we need this?
objections.rebuttal: Google rating is the front door, but AI tools go deeper — they check whether your physicians are individually findable and whether your listings are consistent across the web. {entity_name}’s Google presence is solid; the gap is in {gap_label}.

objections.objection: We rank well on Google — isn’t that enough?
objections.rebuttal: Traditional search and AI recommendation are different systems. AI tools query their own training data and retrieval indexes, not your Google rank. Low entity resolution rate is a gap that doesn’t show up in Google Analytics.

objections.objection: What’s actually blocking the score from improving?
objections.rebuttal: The {ceiling_value}-point ceiling applies when {score_ceiling_reason_plain}. It’s a hard block — no other improvement moves the number until this one issue is resolved.

objections.objection: We’re a group practice — patients choose us, not individual doctors.
objections.rebuttal: That’s shifting. AI tools increasingly surface individual physicians for condition-specific searches. Right now a significant portion of {entity_name}’s physicians have no reviewable online presence — those are search results your competitors can take.

objections.objection: We control our own website — why does it matter what third-party sites say?
objections.rebuttal: AI systems aggregate signals across dozens of listing sources, not just your website. When those sources disagree on your name, address, or phone, AI tools reduce recommendation confidence.

objections.objection: If we’re already showing up well, why ongoing monitoring?
objections.rebuttal: AI recommendation outputs change as models update and competitors improve. {entity_name} is in a strong position today — the work is holding it. Practices can drop significantly in 90 days after a competitor resolves a linkage gap.

objections.objection: We tried something similar before and it didn’t move the needle.
objections.rebuttal: The difference is measurement. We run direct test queries against the AI tools your patients actually use — not an SEO proxy. The entity resolution rate is the exact number we move, re-measured every 90 days.

The ceiling resolves once {score_ceiling_reason_plain}. Physician capture improvements typically appear within 60 days of profile setup. Both are re-measured at the 90-day rerun — you’ll see an exact score delta.

objections.objection: Your ratings and reputation look strong already — why do you need this?
objections.rebuttal: Strong ratings and review counts are table stakes. What separates top AI-recommended providers isn’t just reviews — it’s whether AI tools reliably resolve the entity, link physicians, and attribute the reputation to the right location. Those signals operate below the surface of what looks correct to you.

objections.objection: Our directory listings look fine — what are you actually fixing?
objections.rebuttal: Listings appearing correct from your side and AI tools confidently attributing reviews and queries to you are different things. Clean-looking directories can still produce ambiguous entity resolution in AI models — the structured data layer works differently from what’s visible to a human reviewer.

objections.objection: We don’t control what AI tools say about us — how is this even fixable?
objections.rebuttal: AI tools generate responses based on indexed structured data, review signals, and entity resolution — all of which are directly addressable. This isn’t about influencing AI opinions; it’s about ensuring the right signals are indexed so AI tools can accurately represent you.

objections.objection: We’re already happy with our Google presence — what else is there?
objections.rebuttal: Google search rank and AI recommendation capture are separate systems. AI tools query structured indexes and entity resolution data, not your Google ranking. A practice can rank well on Google and still be underrepresented when patients ask an AI tool for a recommendation.

generic_objections.objection: How is this different from traditional SEO or digital marketing?
generic_objections.rebuttal: Traditional SEO targets search engine rankings. AI tools — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity — pull from structured data, entity resolution indexes, and reputation signals that don’t map to Google ranking factors. AI recommendation is a separate channel with separate signals to optimize.

generic_objections.objection: What does the measurement actually look like?
generic_objections.rebuttal: We run standardized query batteries against the AI tools your patients actually use, capturing whether {entity_name} appears, how it’s described, and whether competitors are named instead. The Pulse Score is the composite of those results — re-measured every 90 days so you can see the exact delta.
